fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. The writer says, "Therefore strengthen your limp hands and weak knees." (Hebrews 12:12) That Therefore points back to the verse before it. Discipline seems painful at the time, but later it yields "a harvest of righteousness and peace" to those who have been trained by it. So when the pain makes you feel limp and weak, the writer says to strengthen up and keep going, because the training pays off later.
